title: States Weekly: August 26, 2026
gist: CSIS's India States Weekly rounds up sub-national policy actions in the week to August 26, 2026: Delhi's EV-only light-goods-vehicle mandate from 2027, Assam's new hydrocarbon exploration policy, multiple state electricity-tariff and grid regulations, investor-friendly business-reform bills, land-pooling and labor-code rules, and a high-density Delhi 2047 master plan.

insights.claim: Delhi will allow only electric N1 light goods vehicles (max 3.5 tons) to be registered from January 1, 2027, extending the rule across the wider National Capital Region from July 1, 2027.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: A hard registration cutoff creates a firm demand floor for commercial EVs in India's capital region, relevant to EV and fleet-electrification plays.
insights.quote: only electric N1 light goods vehicles...will be allowed to be registered in Delhi from January 1, 2027

insights.claim: Assam unveiled a Hydrocarbon Exploration, Production and Upstream Ecosystem Development Policy, 2026 to boost oil and natural gas exploration, particularly in undiscovered areas.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Signals a state-level push to expand upstream oil and gas activity, a potential opening for exploration and services investment in northeast India.

insights.claim: Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh each approved a 6.83 percent average electricity tariff increase for FY2026-27 effective September 1, 2026, while Tripura announced a 100 percent subsidy absorbing its entire tariff hike retroactive to May 2026.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Diverging tariff paths show varied state approaches to power-cost pass-through versus subsidy, affecting utility economics and fiscal burden.
insights.locator: Climate Change and Energy — Jammu and Kashmir / Tripura

insights.claim: Rajasthan now mandates that solar, wind, hybrid, and transmission-corridor projects include afforestation and green-cover plans in project design and long-term land management.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Adds a compliance and land-management cost layer to renewable project development in a key Indian solar/wind state.
insights.quote: It requires solar, wind, hybrid projects and associated infrastructure such as transmission corridors to include plans for afforestation

insights.claim: Andhra Pradesh passed The Omnibus (Speed of Doing Business) Bill, 2026 to ease approvals with an auto-appeal mechanism for delayed public services, revamped fire-safety audits, and a two-tier committee to fast-track industrial clearances.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: A pro-investment regulatory streamlining that could improve Andhra Pradesh's attractiveness for industrial and manufacturing FDI.
insights.quote: It aims to simplify regulations, ease approval procedures and build a more investor-friendly, trust-based regulatory system
insights.locator: Industrial Policy and Business Regulations — Andhra Pradesh

insights.claim: Haryana notified a Diesel Generator Set Subsidy Scheme reimbursing MSMEs 50 percent of a new generator's cost up to INR 20 lakh ($23,800), plus 50 percent up to INR 5 lakh for Retrofit Emission Control Devices.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Subsidy support for backup power reveals persistent grid-reliability gaps for Indian MSMEs, relevant to genset and emission-control suppliers.
insights.locator: Industrial Policy and Business Regulations — Haryana

insights.claim: Assam approved Industrial Relation Rules, 2026 and Social Security Rules, 2026 based on the Union government's Industrial Relations Code, 2020 and Code on Social Security, 2020, replacing colonial-era regulations to streamline labor governance.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: State-level operationalization of India's national labor codes signals continued labor-market modernization relevant to employers and investors.
insights.quote: The rules are based on the Union government’s Industrial Relations Code, 2020
insights.locator: Land Acquisition and Labor Regulations — Assam

insights.claim: Jammu and Kashmir notified a Land Pooling Policy, 2026 requiring developers to secure voluntary consent from at least 70 percent of landowners in a contiguous area before proceeding.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: A consent-threshold framework shapes the feasibility and cost of large-scale development projects in the union territory.
insights.quote: at least 70 percent of the landowners in a contiguous area before proceeding with land pooling schemes
insights.locator: Land Acquisition and Labor Regulations — Jammu and Kashmir

insights.claim: The Union government notified the Master Plan of Delhi 2047 (MPD-2047), allowing high-rise, high-density development in the National Capital.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: A long-horizon densification plan for Delhi is a structural signal for real-estate and construction exposure in the capital.
insights.quote: It allows for high-rise and high-density development in the National Capital.

insights.claim: Maharashtra amended its Government Rules of Business to empower the Chief Minister to override any Minister's decisions when deemed in the public interest with reasons recorded in writing.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Centralization of executive authority in India's most industrialized state signals a shift in state decision-making dynamics.
insights.quote: It empowers the Chief Minister of Maharashtra to override decisions made by any Minister

insights.claim: Karnataka passed Municipal Corporations and Municipalities Amendment Bills creating a legal mechanism to convert 'B-Khata' properties in unauthorized layouts to compliant 'A-Khata' status.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Regularizing unauthorized-layout property titles could unlock development and financing for affected Karnataka real estate.
